itinerary.labelHtml:
The Itinerary

Day by day

Swipe each carousel for CC-attributed photos. Every stop carries cost, June weather/water, money-saving tip, splurge, picky-kid restaurants, backup / if-time ideas, blog links, and a map. Daily costs cover food + activities only, not lodging/flights.

days.heading: Depart Pittsburgh after work
days.note: No nonstop PIT→Split. Recent checks put this around ~14 hours with one connection and about $898–1,053 pp, so treat flights as the fragile budget line.

days.heading: Arrive Split → easy Riva evening

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Airport transfer, Riva, old town edge, optional Bačvice dip

days.note: The win is landing cleanly, not sightseeing hard. Stay near but not inside the palace lanes if luggage/quiet matter.

days.note: This is the one mid-trip boat move replacing Portugal’s internal flight. It also falls on Juneteenth observed, which preserves the 8-PTO math. It's also a shorter, cheaper hop than the old Hvar–Dubrovnik leg would have been — build no major activity around it until exact 2027 sailing times are known.

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Marco Polo House, St. Mark's Cathedral, walls loop, Bilin Žal swim

days.note: Korčula's Old Town is a fraction of Dubrovnik's size and crowds — most of it is free to wander, so this is a deliberately slow, cheap day after two transfer-heavy legs.

spots.name: Korčula Old Town & City Walls
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · KorčulaFlickr

images.alt: Korčula Old Town streets and walls
images.captionTitle: Korčula Old Town streets and walls

spots.climate: 78–81°F day / 65–68°F night. Korčula sea is typically 71–72°F in this Jun 18–22 slot, warming through late June.
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk the free herringbone-pattern streets and walls loop; skip paid interiors if attention spans are short.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Evening Moreška sword-dance show (seasonal, Korčula's own centuries-old tradition) for a genuinely local spectacle the kids will remember.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Pape — pizza/pasta, ~$15–25 pp, 3.9★ — sea-wall terrace, thin-crust pizza, easy plain order.
  • Popina — pizza/ćevapčići, ~$14–22 pp, 3.8★ — eastern seawall, family-friendly, good value.
  • Leo Food — pizza/burgers/hot dogs, ~$8–15 pp, fast — cheapest picky-kid reset on the main pedestrian street.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Bilin Žal ↗ — small in-town pebble beach a 5-minute walk from the walls, the easiest first Korčula swim.
  • Pupnatska Luka ↗ — quieter south-coast cove with a bigger wow factor, but it needs a taxi/car.
  • Badija Island ↗ — short water-taxi ride for monastery, deer, and swim coves.

days.heading: Lumbarda beach day

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Vela Pržina sandy beach, Lumbarda village lunch

days.note: This is the picky-kid payoff day: Korčula Island's best sandy beach, a 15-minute bus ride away, with none of Dubrovnik's beach-club price pressure.

spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Lunch at one of Lumbarda's small Grk white-wine cellars while the kids nap post-swim.

• Pizzeria Pape — pizza/pasta, ~$15–25 pp, 3.9★ — sea-wall terrace, thin-crust pizza, easy plain order.

days.heading: Mljet National Park day trip

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Morning boat to Pomena, salt-lake swim/bike loop, Sveta Marija islet

days.note: Jun 22 is a Croatian public holiday, so book the boat and lunch spot ahead of time and expect more local leisure traffic on the water. This is the nature-heavy payoff day for the whole Korčula leg.

spots.name: Mljet National Park
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · MljetFlickr
spots.cost: 2026 park entrance €25 adult/€8 child (7–18) in high season, family ~$70–80; organized boat day from Korčula (guide, transfers, park entry) roughly $170–250 family before lunch. Bike/kayak rental extra ~€12–35 pp.

spots.saveHtml: Save Skip bike/kayak add-ons and just walk the lakeshore loop and swim; the park entry plus boat already fills the day.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Rent bikes at Pomena/Polače for the full lake loop, including the Sveta Marija islet boat shuttle.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Pape — pizza/pasta, ~$15–25 pp, 3.9★ — good landing-night dinner back in Korčula.
  • Popina — pizza/ćevapčići, ~$14–22 pp, 3.8★ — eastern seawall, family-friendly, good value.
  • Leo Food — pizza/burgers/hot dogs, ~$8–15 pp, fast — pack a picnic on Mljet itself, since Pomena/Polače options are thin.

  • Badija Island ↗ — shorter island outing from Korcula if Mljet ferry timing is awkward.
  • Saplunara Beach ↗ — sandy beach option if the national park lakes feel too structured.

days.heading: Depart Korčula → DBV → PIT

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Korčula → Orebić ferry → Pelješac Bridge → DBV → PIT

days.note: Budget the full ~2.5 hours door to airport: a short car ferry to Orebić, then a fully domestic drive across the Pelješac Bridge to DBV — no Bosnia border crossing. Book the private transfer (~$130–190 family) in advance rather than relying on the public bus/ferry combo on a flight day. Because June 23 is part of the blackout constraint, choose a one-ticket route with a realistic connection.

Getting Around

Flights, one short rental, and ferries

The Croatia version swaps Portugal’s mid-trip flight for ferries and keeps driving tightly scoped to Split day trips.

ReturnDubrovnik / DBV → gateway → PIT

No direct PIT→Split; fastest public routings show connections and roughly ~14 hours. Recent observed fares of ~$898–1,053 pp are the planning anchor. DBV stays the return airport even though the family no longer overnights in Dubrovnik — Korčula's own exit route (below) makes that a clean fit.

Use it for Krka/Trogir/Klis only. Sunday pickup may mean shorter city-office hours; airport pickup is the fallback. Return before Hvar; island ferries and Korčula's tight Old Town streets make a car a liability there.

Krilo and TP Line (plus some Jadrolinija sailings) run direct Hvar–Korčula catamarans Apr–Oct; book once 2027 schedules load. This leg is both shorter and cheaper than the old Hvar–Dubrovnik run.

Plan Health-Check

What to lock, watch, and expect

A critical review of the Croatia plan against the corrected Jun 10–23 travel dates — refreshed July 2026. Kids assumed 13 & 8 in June 2027.

Act now

Flights are the fragile joint

PIT→Split has no direct or near-direct routing. Current public fare checks show no direct flights and roughly ~14-hour fastest routings; your recent fare band of $898–1,053 pp is realistic. Let the open-jaw air ticket set exact dates before locking nonrefundable villas.

Heads-up

Krka is not a waterfall-swim free-for-all

Skradinski buk swimming remains off-limits. Krka permits swimming only in marked zones at Roški slap, Stinice and Pisak from Jun 1–Sep 30, and conditions can still close them. Treat Krka as a boardwalk/waterfall day first.

Fixed

Dubrovnik is gone — and the Pelješac Bridge makes that easy

Korčula replaces Dubrovnik as the final base. The 2022 Pelješac Bridge now connects Korčula/Pelješac straight to the mainland, so the Jun 23 exit to Dubrovnik Airport (DBV) is a domestic ~2.5-hour ferry-plus-drive with zero Bosnia border crossings — the old Neum-corridor delay risk is gone entirely, even without visiting Dubrovnik itself.

Heads-up

Hvar ferries are easy — exact times are not

Split↔Hvar is frequent and short; Hvar↔Korčula runs Apr–Oct on fast catamarans (Krilo, TP Line, some Jadrolinija sailings) and is usually 50 min–1.5 hr / roughly €20–30 pp — a big improvement over the old 3h20m+ Hvar–Dubrovnik leg. Book once 2027 schedules post; skip a mainland car on Hvar or Korčula.

Solid — keep it

The water problem is actually fixed

June Adriatic sea temperatures around Split/Hvar/Korčula run roughly 70–72°F on this earlier mid-June window, warming as the trip moves south. That is a major improvement over the Portugal Atlantic plan’s 63–69°F kid-swim problem.

Every stop below includes pizza/pasta/burger/fries fallbacks with prices and ratings. Croatia is easier than it looks for picky kids as long as you keep plain Italian-style options near each day’s endpoint.

The corrected Jun 10–23 plan uses 8 PTO days because the first date is an after-work departure and Friday Jun 18 is the observed Juneteenth holiday. It returns on Wednesday, June 23. What changed from the old Jun 11–24 draft

The trip is one day earlier overall, so Split starts on Friday Jun 11, Hvar starts Tuesday Jun 15, Korčula starts Friday Jun 18, and the final full day is Tuesday Jun 22. Costs are slightly friendlier than late June/July, but the water is also about a degree cooler at the front of the trip.

Aaron has already been to Dubrovnik, so the final 5-night base is now Korčula Town, with day trips to Pelješac (Ston walls, oysters, wine country) and Mljet National Park (salt-lake swimming). The route still flies home from Dubrovnik Airport (DBV) — that part hasn't changed — but the family never overnights in Dubrovnik itself. See the Where We Stay and Day by Day sections below.

Best overall answer

  • Jun 28–Jul 11 is the strongest all-factor window: 8 PTO, no blackout conflict, warmer water, better lavender, and still before the worst late-July/August pressure.

Why not peak July/August?

Recommendation

Absolute best: Jun 28–Jul 11. It keeps PTO to 8 days, clears the Jun 23–26 blackout, improves swim water and lavender odds, and avoids the worst late-July/August travel pressure. Keep Jun 10–23 only if June 23 can be a travel-home day and lower June costs matter more than warmer water.

Before you go — documents

Months ahead · Schengen rules

  • ETIAS is expected to be operating by June 2027. Official EU guidance says ETIAS starts in Q4 2026 with transitional/grace periods. Use only the official portal once live.
  • EES biometric borders are fully operational as of April 10, 2026. Expect first-entry face/fingerprint registration; under-12s do not give fingerprints.
  • Check passports now. Croatia is Schengen: passports need validity beyond the trip and kids’ passports expire faster.
  • Bring proof of parent/child relationship and notarized consent if one parent is not traveling.

Flights & airports

Booking + day-of

  • No direct PIT→Split. Prioritize one-ticket routings with enough gateway buffer over chasing a tiny fare savings.
  • Pay for seats together on transatlantic legs; do not rely on airport assignment with kids.
  • Use DBV for the return so you do not waste the last day crossing back to Split.
  • Keep transfer days light. Catamarans and summer winds can shift exact timing.

Arrival day — go private

Skip friction on no sleep

  • Pre-book SPU→Split transfer if arriving after a long connection; the bus is cheaper but less forgiving.
  • Do not pick up the rental on arrival. Split old town and jet lag are a bad combo.
  • Choose lodging for luggage access. Old-town charm with stairs is not charming with four bags.

Rental cars & ferries

Keep wheels limited

  • Rent only in Split for Krka/Trogir/Klis. Return before Hvar.
  • Child restraints matter. For an 8-year-old, bring a packable booster if height/fit is borderline; rental seats are inconsistent.
  • Ask rental agencies about ferry permission only if you change plans and take a car to an island.
  • Korčula is not a car base either. Old Town is pedestrianized; use the private driver/tour for the Pelješac day instead of self-driving across the bridge.

Parks & timed tickets

Rules changed in ways families notice

  • Krka: swimming only in marked zones at Roški slap, Stinice and Pisak, Jun 1–Sep 30; not below Skradinski buk.
  • Plitvice: no swimming. It is a world-class boardwalk/hiking day, not the answer to the kid-swimming brief.
  • Mljet: pay the 2026 high-season rate. €25 adult/€8 child (7–18), a return boat to Sveta Marija islet is included.
  • Book the Mljet boat and Pelješac driver 2–4 weeks ahead but keep weather flexibility.

Smart packing

Small things that matter

  • Pack water shoes for rocky Adriatic beaches, Lokrum and Hvar coves.
  • Bring reef-safe sunscreen, hats and lightweight coverups. Shade can be expensive.
  • Carry some cash for beach bars, taxis, lockers and small island vendors.
  • Download offline maps and ferry PDFs before crossing islands.
